unit.title: Inception & “formalize thinly”
unit.moc: the tribunal's vocabulary — the thesis — what it is/is not — the core loop — the name

checkpoint.title: Checkpoint 1 — gate
checkpoint.prompt: Reproduce the vocabulary and the thesis, and name the thing the tribunal is NOT. Write a short verdict.

facts.text: The tribunal's vocabulary runs: *the Living Tribunal* (the system) → *sitting* (one problem) → *quorum* (the multi-model vote) → *convergence* (the verdict). The `hub` CLI is the machinery; the name is the model.

exercises.prompt: One problem run through the tribunal is called a:
The multi-model vote over that problem is the:

facts.text: Formalize THINLY: the value is discipline (independence, grounding, recorded dissent), not machinery. The blueprint document + the intake template + the ledger + the `hub` CLI = the whole system.
The verdict: “formalize — thinly.” The habit already caught a wrong model claim, audited a session report, and shipped a migration blueprint — more validation than most tools get.

exercises.prompt: Formalize thinly means the value is the ___ , not the machinery.
Which of these is NOT part of “the whole system”?
Type the thesis sentence you just heard.
exercises.text: The value is discipline, not machinery.

facts.text: The tribunal takes a problem, routes the SAME brief through independent model lanes, forces them to challenge each other, grounds the result, and returns ONE converged, evidence-cited answer.
It is NOT: a build environment, a chat playground, an agent orchestrator for long-running work, a replacement for reading primary docs, or a destination for lab data or secrets.

exercises.prompt: Which is a true statement about what the tribunal returns?

options: a way to route the same brief to independent lanes
a build environment that returns commits
a way to force lanes to challenge each other

exercises.prompt: Match each scope fact to its side.

facts.text: The core loop: Intake → Triage → Ground → Route (blind) → Converge → Verify → Record. Independence is the product: each lane sees the SAME brief and no lane sees another's output until convergence.
Verify means against the artifact the user runs — run it, grep the repo, read the vendor doc. Never model agreement alone.

exercises.prompt: Put the core loop steps in order.
What does “verify” mean in the loop?
options: checking against the artifact the user runs

facts.text: “Quorum” was real Claude's proposal and it names the property that makes the hub work — you need a quorum of independent voices, not one. “Crossbench” is the runner-up.

exercises.prompt: Which name was recommended, and why?
options: PolyModel Hub — because it is generic
Quorum — because it names the independence property
Sounding Board — because it is evocative
